title: Let LLMs Wander: Engineering RL Environments — Stefano Fiorucci
talk_summary: Stefano Fiorucci explains RL environments for LLM agents using the Verifiers library, walking through single-turn, multi-turn, and tool environments, then trains a small model to master tic-tac-toe via SFT warm-up plus GRPO/CISPO. The practical core is environment engineering: deterministic rewards, seeded rollouts, stratified sampling, controlled opponent difficulty, and inspecting trajectories to catch hidden biases.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each environment bundles weighted reward functions (win, format, invalid-move penalty) computed programmatically against ground truth, so every rollout gets an automatic score without human judgment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We use two reward function, winner reward function with weight one, and format reward function with weight 0.2

takeaways.technique: Seed rollouts to remove environment noise
takeaways.what_they_do: They derive a per-example seed and a per-turn seed from board state so identical states always produce identical opponent responses, isolating model behavior from randomness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if two rollouts reach the same board position, the opponent will always respond the same way

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of random batches, they force every batch to contain a balanced mix of opponent difficulty so average reward doesn't swing and training stays stable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This forces every batch to contain a perfectly balanced mix of opponent difficulty spanning the chosen range.

takeaways.technique: Match model capability to task difficulty
takeaways.what_they_do: They tune opponent skill (random-move probability) so the model sees winnable games early; too-perfect opponents gave no learning signal, and training only against perfect opponents made the model overly defensive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the opponent is too perfect too early, the model might never see a win and fail to learn.

takeaways.technique: Inspect rollouts, not just aggregate scores
takeaways.evidence_quote: Inspecting the rollouts, I found some recurrent failure modes.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before RL, they fine-tune on ~200 filtered synthetic examples from a strong teacher to teach format and valid-move syntax, then use RL for deeper capability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We can use supervised fine-tuning for a warm-up phase, where we teach the model the format and valid moves syntax.
